moment_text: Tonight, you'll climb into bed, close your eyes, and turn yourself off for eight hours.

moment_text: Sleep is the single most dangerous thing you do every single day, and you can't live without it.

moment_text: For thousands of years we had no idea why we did it.

moment_text: Now we're starting to find out, and it's weirder than you think.

moment_text: After two weeks they were all dead.

moment_text: Their immune systems stopped working. Their bodies just gave out.

moment_text: And Rechtschaffen still couldn't tell you exactly why sleep was the thing that killed them.

moment_text: So what is sleep actually doing?

moment_text: For a long time people thought your brain just turned off at night. It doesn't.

moment_text: Your brain is more active during some parts of sleep than it is when you're awake.

moment_text: It cycles about every ninety minutes between deep sleep and REM sleep.

moment_text: Deep sleep is the slow, heavy part, and REM — rapid eye movement — is when you dream.

moment_text: You do both every single night, and both are doing different jobs.

moment_text: Deep sleep is when your brain does its janitorial work.

moment_text: A few years ago scientists discovered something called the glymphatic system

moment_text: — basically a network of tiny pipes that only switches on when you're asleep.
visual_prompt: cutaway view of a brain with glowing blue pipes and valves, lit up ACTIVE sign, moon icon in corner

moment_text: While you're awake, your brain cells are busy, and they produce waste the way every busy factory does.

moment_text: During deep sleep those brain cells literally shrink to make space between them

moment_text: and cerebrospinal fluid washes through in pulses, flushing out all the garbage.

moment_text: Build up too much of it, and you get the plaques associated with Alzheimer's.

moment_text: Every bad night of sleep is a skipped trash day for your brain.

moment_text: Sleep also files your memories.

moment_text: and moves the important ones into long-term storage in the cortex.
